name: MonarchSparkline
title: Sparkline
summary: A word-sized trend line, area or bar chart for tables, stat cards and lists, with a text alternative.
whenToUse: Beside a number, to show where it has been: in a stat card, a table cell or a list row.
whenNotToUse: For a chart people read values from, with axes and a legend, use Swift Charts. Never as the only carrier of a value: show the number or a MonarchDeltaIndicator beside it.
api: MonarchSparkline.init(_ values: [Double?], label: String? = nil, summary: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone? = nil, color: MonarchChartColor? = nil, variant: MonarchSparklineVariant = .line, range: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, isInverted: Bool = false, showsLastPoint: Bool = true, notEnoughDataLabel: String? = nil, fullWidth: Bool = false, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil)

options.name: values
options.description: The values in order. nil, or a value that is not finite, is a gap.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name. Without it the sparkline is decorative and hidden.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the spoken value "latest 9, low 3, high 9".

options.name: tone
options.description: A colour with meaning. nil takes the surrounding foreground style.

options.name: range
options.description: Fixes the value range, so sparklines in a table share one scale.

options.name: isInverted
options.description: Draws smaller values higher, as for a rank.

options.name: showsLastPoint
options.description: Puts a dot on the latest point. Lines and areas only.

options.name: notEnoughDataLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "Not enough data".

options.name: fullWidth
options.description: Fills the available width instead of 80 points.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes the numbers of the spoken value. The default is a number in the current locale.

options.name: color
options.description: A chart series colour (a data slot of the theme); ignored when a tone is set.

states.name: line
states.description: A line that breaks at gaps, with a dot on the latest point and on every point that stands alone.

states.name: area
states.description: The line with a soft fill down to the baseline.

states.name: bar
states.description: One bar per value, from zero; negative values go down.

states.name: not enough data
states.description: Fewer than two values (one for bars): the text "Not enough data".

appearance: Without a tone the line takes the foreground style around it and the area a faint level of the same style. With a tone the line uses the tone's strong colour and the area its subtle colour, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web sizes are pixels; here the sparkline is 80 by 24 points and scales with Dynamic Type, or fills the width. The web tones current and accent, the series colours, the threshold option that picks a tone from the latest value, and markers on all points are not offered: pass the tone you want. The web domain is the range parameter. The chart runs from the leading edge, so it is mirrored in right-to-left layouts and the latest value is at the trailing end; the web one is not mirrored. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: With a label the sparkline is one element with the image trait: the label is its name and the value is "latest 11, low 3, high 11", followed by the name of the tone when it has one.
Without a label it is hidden from VoiceOver, so the numbers must be in text nearby.
The tone is spoken by name, so it does not depend on colour, and the numbers it stands for should be visible beside it.
The "Not enough data" text is read; with a label it becomes the value.
The sparkline scales with Dynamic Type. It does not animate.
edgeCases: A flat series is drawn in the middle of the height.
A value outside a fixed range is drawn at the edge.
Bars always include zero in their range; a zero value is a one-point bar.
A single value between two gaps is drawn as a dot, because a line cannot show it.
